correctness.rationale: In characteristic two, odd m makes T^m-1 square-free and splits the rotation algebra into field factors tensored with F_q[t]/t^4. Inversion swaps the reciprocal-pair blocks; in the nonsplit orbit its order-two action is nontrivial on K=F_(q^{2d}). For theta of relative trace one, w=t+theta(t²+t³) is fixed because inversion fixes t² and t³ and adds t²+t³ to t. As w is a uniformizer, the involution in the w-coordinate acts only on coefficients. The twisted algebra is M2 over F_(q^d)[w]/w^4 by the faithful quadratic Galois action with multiplication; this descent works even in characteristic two. In D8 direct expansion forces a0=b0, a1=0, b1(b0+b1)=0; for b0 nonzero the b-component exhibits an injective four-dimensional column. Otherwise the induced matrix on the t²-layer over F_q[t]/t² is invertible if a2+b2 is nonzero, and has a unit pivot and vanishing determinant if a2=b2 is nonzero. The remaining t³-layer is an ordinary two-dimensional rank calculation. These cases give exactly H_q. In the matrix block L_X acts by X on each column (the 'right multiplication' wording in the proof is a slip). For valuation at least two, ranks follow from the reduction and a single complementary entry. For valuation one, after reducing to J=E12, B=bI+cJ and the pivot t leaves complementary entry t³(C21+b²), giving regular ranks six or eight. For nonzero reduction J, the upper-right entry is a unit; square zero is then exactly zero trace and zero determinant, so x11 in tS and x12 in 1+tS give Q^6 choices per J, and the image has maximum rank. This verifies P_Q coefficient by coefficient. Direct products add ranks, with scalar-degree conversion, so degree 4m and the top coefficient follow with the stated acyclicity criterion. The two frozen C++ checkers were inspected, not executed; their reported exhaustive counts for the named small cases agree and are not the proof for arbitrary parameters.

value.rationale: Square-zero left multiplication makes the labeled regular algebra a chain complex, and its rank determines the dimension of its homology. The all-q and all-odd-m enumerator gives actual multiplicities for every homology dimension and the acyclic case, not just numbers of codes, or isolated ranks from a small experiment. The reciprocal-orbit organization explains how the global census changes with the field and odd part of the group order. No extension to even m or classification up to conjugacy is asserted.
